page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 124 GB of RAM, providing 3.88 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The processor features a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX-512 vector extensions, VAES cryptography, and SHA_NI instructions.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression scoring in the top 10%. Multi-core scaling is strong, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks placing in the top 25%, though stress-ng multi-core performance falls into the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Redis SET operations and database operations, demonstrate average performance. For machine learning workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small 135M models, but drops to average performance for medium 7B models.

From a resource density perspective, the c4d-standard-32 offers a balanced hardware profile that delivers strong single-threaded compute efficiency. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and integrated GPUs means workloads requiring high-speed local caching or hardware-accelerated parallel processing must rely on network-attached storage or alternative instance types. This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, web serving, text processing, and light language model inference.
